ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a single-transistor common-emitter RC-coupled amplifier circuit. The transistor emitter is directly grounded; the base is connected to the input signal Ui through coupling capacitor C1, and is connected to +UCC through bias resistor RB; the collector is connected to +UCC through RC; the output is connected from the collector through coupling capacitor C2 to load RL, and the output voltage U0 is taken across RL. Since C1 and C2 are sufficiently large, in the AC equivalent they can be regarded as short circuits, and the power-supply terminal is AC ground, so the collector AC load is RC in parallel with RL. Reasoning calculation: Given Ui=0.1 V and U0=8 V, the magnitude of the voltage amplification factor is |Au|=U0/Ui=8/0.1=80. The AC load resistance is RC||RL=(2 kΩ×6 kΩ)/(2 kΩ+6 kΩ)=1.5 kΩ. The quiescent base current IBQ=(UCC-UBE)/RB=(12-0.7)/280 kΩ=11.3/280000 A≈40.36 μA. According to the small-signal input resistance approximation formula rbe≈300 Ω+26 mV/IBQ, rbe≈300+0.026/40.36×10^-6≈300+644≈944 Ω is obtained. The magnitude of the voltage gain of the common-emitter amplifier is approximately |Au|=η(RC||RL)/rbe, so η=|Au|·rbe/(RC||RL)=80×944/1500≈50.3, and the approximate value is taken as 50.

The transistor emitter is directly grounded; the base is connected to the input signal Ui through coupling capacitor C1, and is connected to +UCC through bias resistor RB; the collector is connected to +UCC through RC; the output is connected from the collector through coupling capacitor C2 to load RL, and the output voltage U0 is taken across RL. Since C1 and C2 are sufficiently large, in the AC equivalent they can be regarded as short circuits, and the power-supply terminal is AC ground, so the collector AC load is RC in parallel with RL.

Reasoning calculation: Given Ui=0.1 V and U0=8 V, the magnitude of the voltage amplification factor is |Au|=U0/Ui=8/0.1=80. The AC load resistance is RC||RL=(2 kΩ×6 kΩ)/(2 kΩ+6 kΩ)=1.5 kΩ. The quiescent base current IBQ=(UCC-UBE)/RB=(12-0.7)/280 kΩ=11.3/280000 A≈40.36 μA. According to the small-signal input resistance approximation formula rbe≈300 Ω+26 mV/IBQ, rbe≈300+0.026/40.36×10^-6≈300+644≈944 Ω is obtained. The magnitude of the voltage gain of the common-emitter amplifier is approximately |Au|=η(RC||RL)/rbe, so η=|Au|·rbe/(RC||RL)=80×944/1500≈50.3, and the approximate value is taken as 50.
